name: burrow-frontend-debugger
description: Browse merkle's React components, open one in isolation, or find it in the running app. Embeds the target app via the tools/frontend-debugger sidecar and bridges component/CSS reveals into the editor. See docs/architecture/15-frontend-debugger.md.

viewsWelcome.contents:
No React components found. Burrow looks for PascalCase `.tsx`/`.jsx` files under the target frontend's `src/`.
[Set the frontend folder](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%22burrow.frontendDebugger.targetDir%22)

burrow.frontendDebugger.targetDir.description: Absolute path to the target Vite frontend. Empty = auto-detect (<workspace>/nodewatch/frontend if it exists, else the workspace folder).

burrow.frontendDebugger.repoRoot.description: Target repo root (so @shared resolves). Empty = first workspace folder.

burrow.frontendDebugger.backendTarget.description: Live-mode proxy target (the Go backend under debug).

burrow.frontendDebugger.mode.description: Data mode at sidecar boot. Runtime flips via the status bar are ephemeral.

burrow.frontendDebugger.uiPort.description: Debugger UI/API port. Falls back to a free port if taken.

burrow.frontendDebugger.targetPort.description: Embedded target dev-server port. Falls back to a free port if taken.

burrow.frontendDebugger.targetBase.description: Base path the target app is served under (merkle serves from the domain root). Only used when spawning the sidecar — an attached sidecar reports its own base.

burrow.frontendDebugger.runCommand.description: Command that starts YOUR dev server, run verbatim in a terminal for "Open App in Browser" (e.g. npm run dev). Empty = use the built-in instrumented sidecar (overlay pre-injected, zero setup). For the verbatim path, add the Burrow inspector Vite plugin to your config so ⌥-click reveal works.

burrow.frontendDebugger.appUrl.description: URL to open in the browser. Empty = auto (the runCommand dev-server URL, or the sidecar target URL).

burrow.frontendDebugger.autoStartOnCompo.description: Warm-start the dev sidecar in the background when the Components view is revealed, so the first isolate/open is instant. Failures log to the Frontend Debugger output channel.

burrow.frontendDebugger.openMaximized.description: Maximize the editor area (hide side bars and the bottom panel) when the Frontend Debugger panel opens, so it fills the window instead of sitting as a small tab.

burrow.frontendDebugger.designLayout.markdownDescription: When isolating a component, also hide the side bars and bottom panel so the source | preview columns fill the window (Framer-style design mode). Off by default: isolating arranges the columns but leaves your file tree alone, and hiding chrome is **Focus Mode**'s job (`⌘⇧↩`, `Esc` to exit). With this on, `⌘B` / `⌘J` are the only way to bring the chrome back.

burrow.frontendDebugger.tidyTabs.markdownDescription: Keep the isolation workbench to one component's tabs: open the source and stylesheet as preview tabs (self-replacing; your first edit pins them) and close the previous component's when you isolate another. The source, stylesheet and live canvas are one workbench — closing any of the three closes the other two. Tabs with unsaved changes and pinned tabs always survive. Set to `false` to leave every isolated component's tabs open.
